Latin word

schola

schola, scholae f.

noun, first declension

a lecture, a learned talk; one class meeting; a school, especially of rhetoric or philosophy; a lecture

In this lexicon

  • lecture

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1.7–8: scholās Graecōrum mōre habēre; Suet. Tib. 11.3; M-O s.v. class, after Egger

  • lesson

    also used · classical · M-O s.v. class

  • school

    also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.102: quī cum in scholā assēdissent (Lewis & Short); Traupman 31: school (advanced), schola; Andresian p. 42; Traupman 174

  • schola superior: school

    modern

Examples

  • ut jam etiam scholās Graecōrum mōre habēre audērēmus … itaque diērum quīnque scholās, ut Graecī appellant, in totidem librōs contulī

    so that I even dared to give lectures in the Greek manner … so I have gathered the five days’ lectures, as the Greeks call them, into as many booksCic. Tusc. 1.7–8
